$about: GATE-22, 2026-08-06: the persona gate re-run against the fixture after the roster-membership fix. The three reproductions the 2026-08-04 round logged as open were re-executed against the pristine script first (all three exit 0, confirming the finding still stood), then against the fixed one. Every quoted line below is copied from a real run, not paraphrased. The 2026-08-04 round keeps its "fail" and its waiver: that is what was true when it ran, and this round supersedes it as the current reading of the same case and target rather than editing the older one.

$elicitation.$why: This corpus measures whether the tooling conforms - gates, manifests, drift counts. No person was prompted in any of these runs and none was meant to be, so it evidences nothing about whether the standard asks anybody anything. It was never labelled that way, which is how 377 green observations came to read as validation of a product whose central promise is being guided.

observations.evidence: Re-verified 2026-08-06 against a fixture repo (docs/personas.md with a two-name roster, specs/payments/spec.md). The three reproductions from the 2026-08-04 finding were run against the unmodified script first and all three printed `spec-structure: OK (1 spec paths)`, exit 0: (a) `**Serves:** \`Whoever I like\``, a name absent from the roster; (b) a spec with no Serves field whose prose contains the phrase 'for whom'; (c) a correct spec against a roster whose rows had their backticks stripped, which empties the parsed roster. Cause: the check was a three-way OR whose first arm (`hasServes`) accepted any non-placeholder `**Serves:**` string without opening personas.md, so the two roster-aware arms behind it were unreachable. After the fix the same three fixtures exit 1: (a) 'spec-structure: capability specs serving a persona who is not on the roster (R10):' / '  - specs/payments/spec.md   serves "Whoever I like"' / 'The roster in docs/personas.md is the constraint, and it reads: Owner-operator Olga, Agency admin Adam.'; (b) 'spec-structure: capability specs with no persona named (ADR-006 - a spec serves someone):'; (c) 'spec-structure: no persona could be read from the roster in docs/personas.md' / '(3 table line(s) seen under \'## The roster\'). A roster row is'. The roster-parse failure is explicit rather than a silent skip, because an empty roster is what let this hide: every arm is a membership test, so nothing to compare against passes everything. Escape hatches were checked individually and all still hold: no personas.md with no capability specs prints 'spec-structure: OK (0 spec paths) (persona check skipped - no personas.md)' exit 0; a fresh adoption carrying the shipped `standard/docs/personas.md` placeholder roster plus the shipped `capability-spec.template.md` exits 0; capability specs with no roster at all still fail with the pre-existing 'capability specs exist but there is no docs/personas.md roster'; an unfilled `**Serves:** \`<persona from docs/personas.md>\`` is reported as serving nobody rather than as serving a persona of that name. This repo's own five specs still pass: 'spec-structure: OK (7 spec paths)', exit 0. Self-review caught one regression the fix itself introduced and it is fixed and covered here: scoping the `**Serves:**` value to its own line truncated a value that wraps, so a spec naming `Owner-operator Olga` on the continuation line was reported as off-roster, quoting a half-sentence back - reproduced, then fixed by reading on to the lines that continue the value and stopping at the blank line, next `**Field:**`, heading, list or table. Regression cover: tools/clarify-gate-test.mjs grew 16 persona cases (both directions, each hatch, the wrapped value in both verdicts, and a roster and Serves written in another language) and reports 'clarify-gate-test: OK - 52 cases'. Six of those cases were measured to fail against the pre-fix script, so the suite detects a revert rather than passing either way. Full gate set green afterwards, including 'tree-check: OK - one tree, shippable' and, inside standard/, 'self-verify: OK - drift 0 - 100% adopted (70/70), 0 excepted'.
